diagnostic_evidence.quote: Our results bridge matrix/tensor decomposition and function approximation, offering a scalable solution for high-dimensional problems.
In this work, we focus on functions with two variables. The case of functions with three (or more) variables will be considered in the upcoming work.
As shown in the tensor-product quadrature method, we need to compute or estimate $M_1M_2$ function values

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims approximation of functions on high-dimensional hypercubes and a scalable solution for high-dimensional problems, but every definition, theorem and algorithm is restricted to two variables (one coefficient matrix and its matrix CUR decomposition), the N-variable case is explicitly deferred, and the quadrature still requires M_1 M_2 function values. The advertised high-dimensional scope and scalability are not established anywhere in the paper.

failure_location.quote: This paper introduces a novel approach to approximating continuous functions over high-dimensional hypercubes by integrating matrix CUR decomposition with hyperinterpolation techniques.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract and conclusion in terms of bivariate functions and label the N-variable case as future work; the two-dimensional results are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The scope claims of the abstract and conclusion (high-dimensional hypercubes, scalable high-dimensional solution, remedy for the curse of dimensionality) are unsupported; only the bivariate case is covered.
issues.title: Abstract advertises a high-dimensional scope the paper does not treat
issues.why_classification: A substantive advertised promise (high-dimensional applicability) must be withdrawn, but the repair is a local rewriting and the bivariate results, rates and guarantees all survive, so the loss is limited rather than major.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We provided theoretical error bounds, ensuring the approximation quality is controllable and on par with the standard method when the coefficient matrix is low-rank.

issues.failure_explanation: The only bound involving the CUR factorization is Corollary cor:added-1, whose hypothesis demands that the selected submatrix have maximal volume. The two adaptive strategies build index blocks uniformly and are halted by an unanalysed smallest-singular-value heuristic; no result connects that test, or the produced index sets, to any error estimate, and the maximal-volume hypothesis is never shown for them. Hence rigorous control of the approximation quality is derived for neither adaptive algorithm.

failure_location.quote: Theoretical error bounds are derived for both approaches, ensuring rigorous control over approximation quality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the fixed-index/max-volume setting of Corollary cor:added-1 and state explicitly that the adaptive algorithms carry no proved error bound.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of rigorous, controllable approximation quality for the second (adaptive) approach is unsupported, as is the conclusion's claim of controllable quality for both algorithms.
issues.title: Claimed error bounds for both strategies are never proved for the adaptive one
issues.why_classification: A substantive advertised guarantee has to be withdrawn for one of the two proposed strategies, but a recognizably comparable claim survives for the fixed-index strategy and no new proof architecture is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote the Hilbert space on $\mathbb{H}_2^0$ as

issues.failure_explanation: Functions with absolutely summable Fourier coefficients form a proper, non-complete subspace of L^2(H_2^0) under the stated inner product, so the displayed set is not the Hilbert space it is claimed to be; functions with square-summable but not absolutely summable coefficients are excluded. All Sobolev spaces and all error statements are then quantified over this misidentified ambient class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the defining condition by sum |f_hat|^2 < +infinity, i.e. the standard L^2 class, which leaves every later statement valid and widens its scope.
issues.overall_effect: The ambient space of H^alpha and of every approximation result is misdefined: legitimate L^2/H^alpha functions are excluded and the claimed Hilbert-space (completeness) property fails.
issues.title: L2 is defined as the class of absolutely summable Fourier coefficients
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition restores the intended Hilbert space; the method, rate and guarantees of all subsequent results survive (indeed for a larger class), so no content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where for each $n$, the left eigenfunctions $\{\phi_{i_n}^{(n)}\}_{i_n=1}^{+\infty}$ form a orthonormal basis in $L^2([a,b])$

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate is not scale invariant: replacing f by lambda f multiplies the left side by |lambda| while the right side is unchanged, so the bound is false for any class containing a nonzero function. In addition, mere L^2 membership yields no algebraic rate in I_n; a hypothesis of the form f in H^alpha with a factor such as |f|_alpha or ||f||_{H^alpha} is needed for the rate I_n >= (1/epsilon)^{1/alpha}.

failure_location.quote: for a given function $f(x_1,x_2)\in L^2([a,b]^2)$, when for each $n$, $I_n\geq (1/\epsilon)^{1/\alpha}$, one has $\|Ff(x_1,x_2)-f(x_1,x_2)\|_{L^2}\leq \sqrt{2}\epsilon$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the estimate for f in H^alpha with the right-hand side scaled by the corresponding norm/semi-norm of f, keeping the stated rate in I_n.
issues.overall_effect: The quoted comparison estimate cannot justify any truncation size or tolerance and must not be used as evidence for the accuracy of the truncation.
issues.title: Remark states an L2 error bound independent of the size and smoothness of f

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}=\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*$ satisfy the conditions and conclusions of Theorem \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-main} or Corollary \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-corollary-main} with $0<\epsilon<1$

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the product in (3.6) gives coefficients sum_j E(i_1,j)F(i_2,j), i.e. the matrix E F^T, while the matrix to be approximated is E F^*, whose (i_1,i_2) entry contains the conjugate of F(i_2,j). Fourier coefficient matrices of real functions are complex, so F is complex in general and (3.6) does not define the claimed low-rank approximation of Ff; correspondingly the proof identity of Theorem 3.3 replacing the coefficients of F-f by A - E F^* is false for the defined function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Conjugate the F-coefficients in phi_j^(2) (equivalently conjugate phi_j^(2) in (3.6), or replace E F^* by E F^T consistently in the construction and proof).
issues.overall_effect: The constructed F-tilde f is not the approximation induced by A-tilde = E F^*, so the whole error analysis is carried out on an object different from the one defined.
issues.title: Separable formula (3.6) yields the coefficient matrix E F^T, not E F^*
issues.why_classification: A single conjugation restores the intended construction and its identity with A-tilde = E F^*; no claim, rate or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For clarity, we set that $\alpha=2$, $C=1$, $\epsilon=1e-7$ and $|f(x_1,x_2)|_{\alpha}=1$. It follows from Theorem \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} that $(I_1,I_2)=(3163,3163)$.

issues.failure_explanation: A matrix in C^{(2I_1+1) x R} is of full column rank only if R <= 2I_1+1 (and similarly for F), yet the prescribed R = ceil(72 ln(2(I_1+I_2)+3)/epsilon^2) exceeds min{2I_1+1,2I_2+1} throughout large parts of the stated range (e.g. for every epsilon<1 when I_1,I_2 are small, and always in the paper's own setting I_n=3163, epsilon=1e-7, which gives R of order 10^16). The omitted hypothesis R <= min{2I_1+1,2I_2+1} makes the asserted existence of such E and F false in these regimes.

failure_location.quote: there exist two full column rank matrices $\mathbf{E}\in\mathbb{C}^{(2I_1+1)\times R}$ and $\mathbf{F}\in\mathbb{C}^{(2I_2+1)\times R}$ such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Cap the rank, e.g. replace R by min{R, min{2I_1+1,2I_2+1}}, or drop 'full column rank' and require only that E F^* have rank at most R.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.3 (and the full-column-rank factorization assumed again in Section 4) is vacuous exactly in the small-matrix and high-accuracy regimes that the paper uses.
issues.title: Theorem 3.3 asserts full column rank factors of width R that need not exist
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate parameter-regime fix: capping R at the trivial rank bound leaves the construction, the rate and every conclusion unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the proof is complete by combining Theorems \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} and \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-main}.

issues.failure_explanation: The only input for the truncation term is Theorem 3.1, which gives min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}; since min <= max, this is strictly weaker than the stated max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha} when I_1 != I_2, so the proof yields a different (larger) term than claimed. The claim is actually false: for f with a single nonzero coefficient at frequency (I_1+1, 0) and I_2 much larger than I_1, ||Ff-f||_{L^2} = |f_hat| while max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha = (I_1+1)^alpha I_2^{-alpha}|f_hat|, so no C independent of {I_1,I_2} can exist.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha} by min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha} in Theorem 3.3 and Corollary cor:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: The anisotropic accuracy statement of Theorem 3.3 is false, and Corollary cor:added-1 repeats the same wrong rate.
issues.title: Truncation term of Theorem 3.3 uses max{I1,I2} where only min{I1,I2} is available
issues.why_classification: The local correction restores exactly what Theorem 3.1 supplies; the method, the alpha-order rate and the isotropic regime used in all experiments are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: By Parseval the squared L2 norm of the difference equals sum |A - E F^*|^2, i.e. exactly ||A - E F^*||_F^2, and ||M||_F <= ||M||_max is false (the generic relation is ||M||_F <= sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) ||M||_max). Theorem 3.2 therefore yields at best sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) epsilon ||A||_2. The stated term is genuinely unattainable: a coefficient matrix with p unit singular values concentrated on a central p x p block of frequencies, with p = ceil((log I)^2) and I_1 = I_2 = I, has best rank-R Frobenius error sqrt(p-R) of order log I (since R = Theta(log I) < p), whereas C max{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha + epsilon||A||_2 tends to 0 as I grows. Corollary cor:added-1 uses the same invalid conversion of a max-norm bound into an L2 bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate both bounds with the Frobenius error of the coefficient matrix, i.e. with sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) epsilon ||A||_2 and sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) sqrt(1+S_2) sqrt(1+S_2/(S_1-S_2+1)) sigma_{S_2+1}(A); keeping the original accuracy then forces epsilon down by this factor and hence R = Theta((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1) epsilon^{-2} log(.)).
issues.overall_effect: The dimension-free accuracy terms of Theorem 3.3 and Corollary cor:added-1 are false; the joint guarantee of logarithmic rank together with epsilon||A||_2 accuracy is impossible, so the central claim of reducing the number of integrals/coefficients 'without compromising precision' has no theoretical support.
issues.title: Max-norm coefficient error is used as an L2 error bound without the dimension factor
issues.why_classification: Every complete repair either multiplies the error term by sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)), destroying the dimension-free accuracy guarantee, or raises the required rank to order of the full matrix size, destroying the low-rank/complexity guarantee; the counterexample shows that no version with the stated rank and accuracy can survive, so the central guarantee materially worsens.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the rank of $\mathbf{G}\in\mathbb{C}^{S_2\times S_1}$ is less than or equal to $R$ with $\min\{S_1,S_2\}> R$

issues.failure_explanation: C has S_2 columns and R has S_1 rows, so phi^(1)_{j_1} = C(i_1,j_1) forces 1 <= j_1 <= S_2 and phi^(2)_{j_2} = R(j_2,i_2) forces 1 <= j_2 <= S_1, while the displayed sum runs j_1 to S_1 and j_2 to S_2; for S_1 != S_2 (the generic case, where Section 4.1 takes S_1 >= S_2) the formula references out-of-range entries and is undefined. The same passage is also inconsistent about G: the preamble declares G in C^{S_2 x S_1} while (4.3) defines G(s_1,s_2) in C^{S_1 x S_2}; with the preamble's shape the product C G^dag R is not conformable either.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt one shape convention (G in C^{S_1 x S_2} as in (4.3)) and write the sum as sum_{j_1=1}^{S_2} sum_{j_2=1}^{S_1}, or transpose G together with both index ranges.
issues.overall_effect: The basic approximation formula underlying both algorithms and the CUR-based function used in Corollary cor:added-1 is ill-defined whenever S_1 != S_2.
issues.title: CUR function formula (4.2) has summation ranges inconsistent with the shapes of C and R
issues.why_classification: Aligning the index ranges and matrix shapes is a local fix that restores the intended identity A-tilde = C G^dag R and leaves every conclusion unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the approximation $\widetilde{F}f(x_1,x_2)$ is obtained according to (\ref{t-lasso:approximation-expression-general-v2-main}) with $S_n=2Kb_n+1$ with $n=1,2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The block formula is written for k >= 1, but the pseudocode evaluates it with k = 0 in the first pass (k is incremented only at the end of the body). At k = 0 the formula gives T'_n = [0 : b_n-1] union [-b_n+1 : 0], which contains the already selected index 0 and only 2b_n-1 new indices. The duplicated index makes C, R (and G) contain a repeated column/row, so their smallest singular value is exactly 0 and the tolerance test is triggered immediately; the stated output size S_n = 2Kb_n+1 and the per-iteration cost 2b_2(2I_1+1)+2b_1(2I_2+1) also presuppose 2b_n fresh indices per iteration. The identical loop template is used in t-lasso:alg2-main and t-lasso:alg1:app-main.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Start the counter at k = 1 (or evaluate the block formula at k+1) so that the blocks are plus/minus [1,b_n], [b_n+1,2b_n], ..., disjoint from {0}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the index blocks of all three algorithms are mis-constructed: the first iteration duplicates the seed index, corrupts the stopping test and violates the stated output sizes and cost counts.
issues.title: Adaptive loops start at k=0 and re-select the seed index in the first block
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and reproduces exactly the disjoint blocks, output sizes and cost counts already stated in the text; the method and its guarantees are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d), where $0<\tau<1$ is a given parameter.

When $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is satisfied, the core matrix $\mathbf{U}$ is obtained as $\mathbf{U}=\mathbf{G}^\dag$

issues.failure_explanation: The specification continues until both ratios are small (max{sigma_min(C)^2/nF_C, sigma_min(R)^2/nF_R} < tau^2, i.e. both C and R have stopped gaining rank), whereas the pseudocode stops as soon as one of them is small (min{...} <= tau). These are mathematically different stopping rules: the pseudocode can halt while sigma_min(R)/sqrt(nF_R) is still large, i.e. while new rows of R are still adding rank/information. The source contains two coherent but incompatible specifications and never decides which one governs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix one stopping rule and state it identically in the prose and the pseudocode (e.g. use max{sigma_min(C)^2/nF_C, sigma_min(R)^2/nF_R} < tau^2 in both places).
issues.overall_effect: The output size, the integral/operation counts and the quality of the produced CUR factors depend on which criterion is used, so Algorithm 1 is not well defined as stated.
issues.title: Stopping test of Algorithm 1 contradicts its own specification (min versus max)
issues.why_classification: Making the two specifications agree is a short local fix that preserves the method and every stated size/cost formula; only the (currently ambiguous) stopping semantics has to be chosen.

Summing the stated expression over k=1,...,K does not equal the S_1S_2 = (2Kb_1+1)(2Kb_2+1) entries of G, so the 'Therefore' that derives the total integral count does not follow from the given breakdown.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 4(k^2-1)b_1b_2 by 4(2k-1)b_1b_2 in the breakdown and re-derive the total (which then reproduces S_1S_2 core integrals plus the stated C and R part).
issues.overall_effect: The per-iteration integral count of Algorithm 2 is false and the derivation of its total count is invalid, even though the total quoted at the end happens to be the correct one.
issues.title: Per-iteration integral count for Algorithm 2 is wrong and does not yield the stated total

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $f(\cdot,\cdot)$ be a continuous periodic function of two variables $x_1$ and $x_2$ over the square

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.1 requires f in H^alpha and its bound contains the unknown semi-norm |f|_alpha and the constant C, yet the section simply sets |f|_alpha = C = 1. For the kink function f_1 this is impossible: its coefficients obey f_hat_(k1,k2) ~ (k1 k2)^{-2} (with f_hat_(k1,0) ~ k1^{-2}), so sum (1+||k||^4)|f_hat|^2 diverges and f_1 is not in H^2 with |f_1|_2 = +infinity. Moreover f_2 and f_3 violate the standing periodicity assumption (e.g. f_2(pi,x_2) != f_2(-pi,x_2)). Hence the derivation of (I_1,I_2) = (3163,3163) and of the advertised epsilon = 1e-7 accuracy is unsupported for the tested functions.

failure_location.quote: For clarity, we set that $\alpha=2$, $C=1$, $\epsilon=1e-7$ and $|f(x_1,x_2)|_{\alpha}=1$. It follows from Theorem \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} that $(I_1,I_2)=(3163,3163)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use test functions inside the stated class (or take alpha < 3/2 for f_1 and periodize f_2, f_3), compute or bound the true semi-norms and constants, and re-derive the truncation sizes and guaranteed tolerance from Theorem 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: The truncation parameters and the claimed accuracy level of all experiments are unjustified, and the theoretical error control of Theorem 3.1 does not apply to the reported test cases.
issues.title: Experimental truncation size is derived outside the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained re-optimization of the experimental parameters (new I_n and a re-run), and the advertised 1e-7 accuracy for these functions must be withdrawn, but the method and the empirical comparison remain recognizably intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When we set $\mathbf{G}_{1k}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{2k}$ as the zero matrix, a simplified version for Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main} is summarized in Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg1:app-main}.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 4 forms the same matrices C and R over the same index sets as Algorithm 2, so the coefficients it must evaluate are the same union {(k_1,k_2): k_1 in [-I_1,I_1], k_2 in T_2} union {k_1 in T_1, k_2 in [-I_2,I_2]}, of size (2I_1+1)S_2 + (2I_2+1)S_1 - S_1S_2. The claimed count subtracts the whole S_1S_2 overlap twice although only the 1 + 4K b_1 b_2 diagonal-block entries are computed as G (not K b_1 b_2), so the claimed strict saving is false: the total equals, not falls below, the count for Algorithms 1 and 2.

failure_location.quote: that is, the number of double integrals in Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg1:app-main} is less than Algorithms \ref{t-lasso:alg1-main} and \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recount the coefficients (total (2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2, of which 1+4Kb_1b_2 are produced during the iterations) and withdraw the strict-comparison claim.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised advantage of the modified algorithm (fewer double integrals) is unsupported; its true integral cost coincides with that of Algorithms 1 and 2.
issues.title: Appendix C wrongly claims Algorithm 4 evaluates fewer integrals than Algorithms 1 and 2
issues.why_classification: The recount itself is contained, but the advertised claim that Algorithm 4 needs fewer integrals than Algorithms 1 and 2 cannot be preserved in any form and must be dropped, so the repair loses a substantive (efficiency) claim.
